claims.text: What the image looks like Dilated CBD with stone in distal duct → choledocholithiasis
claims.quote: Dilated CBD with stone in distal duct Choledocholithiasis

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Ultrasound: dilated CBD >6 mm (>10 mm post-cholecystectomy) → choledocholithiasis / obstruction → MRCP / ERCP
claims.quote: Dilated CBD >6 mm (>10 mm post-cholecystectomy) Choledocholithiasis / obstruction MRCP / ERCP
claims.locator: Non-Trauma Ultrasound Findings, Abdomen / Pelvis table

claims.text: Ultrasound may show gallbladder stones and occasionally CBD stones (less accurate); the CBD is dilated (> 6 mm with the gallbladder intact; > 10 mm after cholecystectomy); undilated ducts early suggest the stones have passed
claims.quote: Ultrasound may show stones in the gallbladder and occasionally in the common bile duct (less accurate). The common bile duct is dilated (> 6 mm in diameter if the gallbladder is intact; > 10 mm after a cholecystectomy). If the ducts are not dilated early in the presentation (eg, first day), stones have probably passed.

claims.text: If doubt exists, MRCP is highly accurate for retained stones; ERCP if MRCP is equivocal (diagnostic and therapeutic); CT is less accurate than ultrasound but can detect liver abscesses and duct dilation
claims.quote: If doubt exists, MRCP is highly accurate for retained stones. ERCP with or without endoscopic ultrasound is performed if MRCP is equivocal; ERCP can be therapeutic as well as diagnostic. CT, though less accurate than ultrasound, can detect liver abscesses and bile duct dilation.

claims.text: Labs: elevated bilirubin and particularly alkaline phosphatase, ALT and GGT are consistent with extrahepatic obstruction
claims.quote: Elevated levels of bilirubin and particularly alkaline phosphatase, alanine aminotransferase, and gamma-glutamyltransferase are consistent with extrahepatic obstruction, suggesting stones, particularly in patients with features of acute cholecystitis or cholangitis.

claims.text: Causes In industrialized countries, > 85% of common duct stones form in the gallbladder and migrate to the bile ducts; most are cholesterol stones
claims.quote: In industrialized countries, > 85% of common duct stones form in the gallbladder and migrate to the bile ducts; most are cholesterol stones.

claims.text: Partial obstruction → biliary colic; more complete obstruction → duct dilation, jaundice and eventually ascending cholangitis; stones obstructing the ampulla can cause gallstone pancreatitis
claims.quote: Biliary colic occurs when the ducts become partially obstructed. More complete obstruction causes duct dilation, jaundice and, eventually, ascending cholangitis with bacterial infection. Stones that obstruct the ampulla of Vater can cause gallstone pancreatitis, the most common cause of acute pancreatitis (2).

claims.text: Symptoms Suspect common duct stones with biliary colic, unexplained jaundice, and/or elevated alkaline phosphatase and GGT
claims.quote: Suspect common duct stones if patients have biliary colic, unexplained jaundice, and/or elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyltransferase levels.

claims.text: Suspect acute cholangitis (a surgical emergency) with abdominal pain, jaundice, and fever or chills
claims.quote: Suspect acute cholangitis (a surgical emergency) in patients with abdominal pain, jaundice, and fever or chills.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: ERCP
If biliary obstruction is suspected, ERCP and sphincterotomy are necessary to remove the stones
claims.quote: If biliary obstruction is suspected, ERCP and sphincterotomy are necessary to remove the stones.

claims.text: Acute cholangitis: aggressive supportive care, antibiotics and urgent stone removal and drainage (endoscopic or surgical)
claims.quote: Acute cholangitis is an emergency requiring aggressive supportive care and urgent stone removal and drainage, endoscopically or surgically (3). Antibiotics are given, similar to those used for acute cholecystitis (see Acute Cholecystitis: Treatment).
